newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico reopens Gulf crude export ports - officials.
newsitem.headline: Mexico reopens Gulf crude export ports - officials.

text.p: Mexico's three Gulf of Mexico crude export ports have all reopened after being closed Monday because of strong winds, port capitans and port pilots said Tuesday.

Pajaritos port in Veracruz state reopened at 0800 local/1400 GMT, Dos Bocas port in Tabasco state restarted shipping movements at 0700 local/1300 GMT and Cayo Arcas in Campeche reopened Monday afternoon, officials said.
"We reopened at 0800 this morning," said an official from Pajaritos port, the second largest export point for crude from the state-owned oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
"Winds died down to normal levels and the port opened at 0700," said an official from the Port Pilots office at Dos Bocas.
Cayo Arcas reopened to shipping late Monday, Capt. Jorge Rios MacBeth told Reuters. He said the neighbouring port of Ciudad del Carmen resumed movements Tuesday at 0800 local/1400 GMT.
All three ports had been forced to curtail shipping movements as strong winds up to 50 km/h were whipped up while a cold front passed through the Gulf of Mexico.
